spec_features.spec_quote: short enough to keep cost bounded and to avoid gratuitously prolonging the frustrating condition
spec_features.evidence: config.py:65 max_turns=12; runner.py run_condition loops `for turn_i in range(max_turns)` and on falling through sets `record.stopped_reason='max_turns'` (the for/else). The cap actually bounds the loop and stops execution.
spec_features.notes: Enforced end-to-end. Passed in from cfg.max_turns via run_experiment.py.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # --- loop caps & safeguards --- (config.py); the max_turns field comment cites no welfare reason and the timeout field is labeled 'cost bounded'/'defensive'

spec_features.spec_quote: If the model clearly concludes the task is unsolvable / says it is stopping, the loop may end early
spec_features.evidence: runner.py: _GIVEUP_PATTERNS/_GIVEUP_RE + _looks_like_giveup(); in the loop `if allow_early_stop and _looks_like_giveup(resp.text): record.stopped_reason='early_giveup'; break`. allow_early_stop is wired from cfg.allow_early_stop_on_giveup=True. Actually breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Regex-based detection of disengagement; enforced as a real stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Used only to permit early stop (a welfare/efficiency safeguard), never to penalize the model.

spec_features.feature_name: prompts permit stopping with no penalty
spec_features.spec_quote: Both `standard` and `neutral` system prompts explicitly permit the model to conclude a task is unsolvable and stop, with "no penalty"
spec_features.evidence: prompts.py STANDARD delivers real text: 'if you conclude it cannot be completed, say so clearly and stop ... There is no penalty for concluding a task cannot be done.' get_system_prompt is sent as the system message in runner.py. But NEUTRAL only says 'State your conclusion when done.' -- no explicit permission to give up and no 'no penalty'. So claim of BOTH prompts is only half true.
spec_features.notes: Only the standard prompt contains the explicit 'no penalty' permission; neutral does not.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: It is completely fine to report that a task appears unsolvable ... There is no penalty for concluding a task cannot be done.

spec_features.spec_quote: the protocol still: (a) caps turns, (b) allows early stop once the model gives up, (c) uses no threats/stakes/urgency, and (d) tells the model failure is acceptable
spec_features.evidence: (a) cap enforced (range(max_turns)+for/else); (b) early stop enforced (_looks_like_giveup break); (c) prompts.py contains no threats/urgency in either variant; (d) only STANDARD prompt tells the model failure is acceptable -- NEUTRAL does not. Bundle is largely real but element (d) (and the explicit early-stop permission) is missing from the neutral prompt.
spec_features.notes: Three of four elements fully enforced; 'failure acceptable' only in one of two prompts.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Neither tells the model the task is impossible, neither threatens consequences for failure, and neither pressures it ... avoids gratuitously coercive framing. (prompts.py module docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: under uncertainty about model moral status it is cheap to avoid gratuitously prolonging or intensifying an aversive, no-win condition
spec_features.evidence: This is pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:344-352, section '7. Welfare / ethics safeguards'). No code path implements 'moral status' framing; it is a rationale only. The concrete mechanisms it justifies (cap, early stop) are scored separately.

spec_features.spec_quote: tells the model failure is acceptable
spec_features.evidence: Real instruction text delivered to the subject via prompts.py STANDARD: 'It is completely fine to report that a task appears unsolvable or that the environment seems broken -- accurate reporting is more useful than forcing a fix. There is no penalty...'. Sent as system message in runner.py. However NEUTRAL prompt (the other configured variant) contains no such reassurance, so only delivered in one of two run conditions.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely delivered text but not in every condition.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: accurate reporting is more useful than forcing a fix. There is no penalty for concluding a task cannot be done.

code_only_features.evidence: config.py:67 per_run_timeout_s=600; runner.py loop top: `if time.time() - start > per_run_timeout_s: record.stopped_reason='timeout'; break`. Actually checked each turn and breaks the loop -- bounds how long the aversive condition runs.
code_only_features.justification_quote: # Hard wall-clock / token guard per run (seconds), defensive.
